unite_adi: UPPER SECONDARY-PREP YEAR-LEVEL: B1 - THEME 12: FAMILY LIFE AND THE FUTURE

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students write and design a project on ''Family Members’ Future Aspirations, Dreams, and Ambitions.'' They will describe the ideal aspirations and ambitions of family members, including the roles each person plays in supporting these dreams, the skills needed, and the actions taken to achieve these goals. They will write scripts for each role, illustrating how each family member works toward their individual aspirations, whether it’s academic success, career goals, or personal growth. In the class, they will act out these roles, showcasing the importance of support, motivation, and effort in achieving their dreams. The assignment will be evaluated using rubrics. bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''family life and the future with its components such as family members’ future aspirations; family members’ dreams and ambitions'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school may know what family members’ future aspirations, family members’ dreams and ambitions mean in their own language as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in another language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''family life and the future'' in English from previous themes and/or years such as ''a father, mother, sister, brother, hope, to achieve, etc.'' and also some structures such as ''My father has improved his skills at engineering a lot. Her sister can work in her dream job when she finishes university.'' in English from the previous themes and/or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school are ready to learn the concept of ''family members’ future aspirations; family members’ dreams and ambitions'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Therefore, a contextual family poster could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss the poster in pairs and write down what they remember. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and /or a marking scheme during these practices.).
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To talk about hypothetical situations in family life in English by practicing target vocabulary and grammar in speaking skills. Activity 1: What If? Debate Activity The teacher introduces a ''What If?'' Debate activity where students work in small groups. Each group is given a hypothetical family scenario written on a card, such as, ''If your parents won the lottery, what would they do?'', or ''If your sibling could study abroad, where would they go and why?''. Students discuss the scenario using target vocabulary and target grammar, such as ''If my parents won the lottery, they would buy houses to secure our future''. Groups then present their ideas to the class. The teacher provides feedback on grammar, vocabulary and presentation skills. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity. Objective: To talk about hypothetical situations in family life in English by using the target grammar through reading comprehension and discussion. Activity 2: What If Stories The teacher provides a short reading passage titled ''What If?'' about a family imagining different scenarios, such as winning the lottery, moving abroad, or starting a family business. After reading the passage, students answer comprehension questions that require them to identify and analyse unreal conditional sentences in the text. For example: ''If the family had moved abroad, how would their lives have changed?'', ''What would they do if they had unlimited time and money?''. Students then work in pairs to create their own hypothetical scenarios inspired by the reading. They present these scenarios to the class by using target grammar, and the teacher and other students provide feedback on their language use and creativity. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To talk about family members’ dreams and aspirations in English by using the target grammar. Activity 1: The teacher gives a worksheet with visuals and incomplete unreal conditional sentences. Each sentence has a related image above it, and students use a word bank to complete the blanks. For example, above the sentence (''If my father had a lot of money, he would __________''), there is a picture of a luxury car. Students choose the correct phrase from the word bank, such as ''buy a luxury car'' and write it in the blank. Other examples include a girl with a travel map for ''If my sister had enough money, she would __________''. (answer: travel the world), and a boy holding a puppy for ''If my brother were a vet, he would __________''. (answer: help animals). After finishing, students share their answers, and the teacher provides feedback. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity. Objective: To talk about family members’ dreams and aspirations in English by using the target grammar. Activity 2: Family Fortune Game The teacher organises a ''Family Fortune Game'' where students work in pairs. Each pair receives a set of cards with incomplete unreal conditional sentences and matching picture cards. For example, a card might read, ''If my mother had more time, she would __________'', and a corresponding picture card shows a woman painting. Students discuss and select the most suitable phrase from a word bank (e.g., ''paint pictures, read books, travel to Paris''). They complete the sentence verbally and match it to the picture. After discussing in pairs, each pair shares their completed sentences with the class, explaining their choices. The teacher provides feedback on grammar and vocabulary, encouraging accuracy and fluency. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
